title: Floquet Green's functions for lattice electrons driven by Gaussian quantum light
abstract: We formulate Floquet Green's functions for noninteracting single-band lattice electrons driven by a reservoir-stabilized single-mode Gaussian quantum light source. The source is prescribed externally and is not updated by the many-electron polarization, while an active electronic probe still conditions the source evolution through the Peierls coupling. The two time arguments of a Green's function share one source history: the lesser and greater components are obtained by convolving a shared-history four-endpoint kernel with the continuous bath kernels before the final source trace, while the bath canonical anticommutation relation yields an equal-time covariance that seeds the retarded and advanced one-leg propagations. The Peierls coupling is treated nonperturbatively within the prescribed-source model, and classical Floquet theory is recovered in the appropriate limit. Numerical calculations on a minimal one-dimensional model show finite-coupling quantum-source corrections beyond a prescribed classical drive, together with spectral reconstruction and occupancy redistribution for squeezed vacuum and squeezed coherent sources. The squeezing parameter and phase provide additional control knobs, beyond classical amplitude modulation, for both sideband structure and occupied weight. This work provides a theoretical framework for quantum Floquet engineering of condensed matter with an externally prescribed quantum light source.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous theoretical framework for studying lattice electrons driven by external, nonclassical quantum light fields. It formulates Floquet Green's functions using a shared-history approach that treats the full quantum nature of the driving source nonperturbatively. The results demonstrate how squeezing and phase control can engineer electronic properties beyond what classical laser drives allow.
main_problem: The primary goal is formulating Floquet Green's functions for noninteracting lattice electrons driven by an externally prescribed, reservoir-stabilized Gaussian quantum light source.
main_result: The work provides a theoretical framework for quantum Floquet engineering of condensed matter systems using external quantum light sources, showing finite-coupling quantum corrections beyond classical drives.
method: It employs a shared-history formulation for two-time Green's functions, treating the nonperturbative Peierls coupling and incorporating bath convolutions derived from canonical anticommutation relations.
model_or_system: The system consists of noninteracting single-band lattice electrons coupled to an external Gaussian quantum light source (reservoir) via the Peierls mechanism. The electron bath provides local linewidths, while the source is modeled as a squeezed coherent steady state.
key_observables: Spectral reconstruction and occupancy redistribution are key observables, which can be controlled by the squeezing parameter and phase of the input light.
important_parameters: The squeezing parameter ($r$) and phase ($\phi_0$) of the quantum source provide control knobs beyond classical amplitude modulation. The coupling strength ($\lambda$) is also critical.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include noninteracting single-band electrons, a prescribed (non-backacting) external light source, and the validity of Gaussian approximations for expectation values involving the Peierls exponentials.
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides an overview diagram illustrating the components: electron–photon system, electron bath, photon source reservoir, and the shared-history construction process involving four active-leg sectors.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by defining the coupled Hamiltonian, deriving the Green's function structure using a shared-history approach, treating the Peierls coupling nonperturbatively, and concluding with numerical demonstrations on a 1D model showing quantum corrections.
why_interesting: This bridges advanced topics in Floquet engineering (time periodicity) with open quantum systems theory (reservoir/bath dynamics) by incorporating the full quantum nature of the driving field (squeezing), which is highly relevant to modern AMO and quantum optics research.
